332446.title: Conjectural structure of lines in GC_n sets
332446.literal_statement:
Assume the Gasca–Maeztu conjecture holds for all degrees up to $\nu$. Let $\mathcal X$ be a $GC_n$ set with $n\leq\nu$, and let $\ell$ be a line passing through exactly $k$ nodes of $\mathcal X$. Write $\mathcal X_\ell$ for the nodes of $\mathcal X$ that use $\ell$ in their fundamental polynomials. A maximal line is a line containing $n+1$ nodes of $\mathcal X$.

**Conjecture concerning $GC_n$ sets.** There is an integer $s$ with $2k-n-1\leq s\leq k$ such that

$$
|\mathcal X_\ell|=\binom{s}{2}.
$$

Moreover, for every maximal line $M$ of $\mathcal X$:
1. $|M\cap\mathcal X_\ell|=0$ if $M\cap\ell\notin\mathcal X$, or if there is another maximal line $M'$ such that $M\cap M'\cap\ell\in\mathcal X$;
2. $|M\cap\mathcal X_\ell|=s-1$ for every remaining maximal line.

This is a structural conjecture about how nodes using a given line are distributed among maximal lines. Its validity is conditional on the Gasca–Maeztu conjecture through degree $\nu$; the source provides no resolution.

332504.title: Characterization conjecture for universal classes of unlabeled robot systems
332504.literal_statement:
Let $G_i$ be unlabeled networks, let $k\geq 3$, and let $\mathcal F(G_i,k)$ denote the corresponding system of $k$ oblivious mobile robots. Let $G_i^\ast$ be the quotient graph associated with $G_i$, and call a set of systems universal when it can simulate every finite computation in the model considered. **Characterization conjecture.** The set

$$
\left\\{\mathcal F(G_i,k)\mid i\geq 0\right\\}
$$

is universal if and only if either the quotient graphs $G_i^\ast$ have unboundedly long sub-paths, or the graphs $G_i$ have unboundedly long shortest cycles.

This conjecture proposes that the two structural conditions identified by the preceding universality results exactly characterize universal classes of systems with at least three robots on unlabeled networks. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

332627.title: The graph-generalized Orlik–Terao conjecture
332627.literal_statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a simple connected graph with vertex set $[n]$, let $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)\subset S_n$ be its automorphism group, and let $OT_\Gamma$ be the Orlik–Terao algebra of the associated graphic arrangement. Define

$$
M_\Gamma:=OT_\Gamma\otimes_{R_n}\mathbb{C}.
$$

Let $D_\Gamma:=H^*(\operatorname{Conf}(\Gamma,G)/G;\mathbb{C})$, where $G$ is the group used in the source, and let $\hat{\Gamma}$ be the cone over $\Gamma$; write $C_\Gamma:=H^*(\operatorname{Conf}(\Gamma,\mathbb{R}^3))$.

**The graph-generalized Orlik–Terao conjecture.** For any simple connected graph $\Gamma$, there exists an isomorphism

$$
M_\Gamma\cong D_\Gamma
$$

of graded representations of $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)$. In particular, there exists an isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Res}^{\operatorname{Aut}(\hat{\Gamma})}_{\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)}(M_{\hat{\Gamma}})\cong C_\Gamma.
$$

This extends the main conjecture from complete graphs to graphic arrangements and configuration spaces associated with arbitrary simple connected graphs. The source gives no resolution.

335792.title: Fair splitting into arbitrarily many stable sets for colored paths
335792.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be a positive integer, and let $P$ be a path whose vertex set is partitioned into $m$ subsets $V_1,\ldots,V_m$, each of size at least $q-1$. A subset of vertices is **$q$-stable** if no two of its vertices are at distance less than $q$, with distance counted in edges.

**Fair stable-set splitting conjecture.** There always exist pairwise disjoint $q$-stable sets $S_1,\ldots,S_q$ covering all vertices but $q-1$ in each $V_j$, with sizes differing by at most one, and satisfying

$$
|S_i\cap V_j|\geq \left\lfloor \frac{|V_j|+1}{q}\right\rfloor-1
$$

for all $i\in[q]$ and all $j\in[m]$.

This conjecture extends the paper's two-independent-set theorem to an arbitrary number of sets: when $q=2$, $q$-stable sets are precisely independent sets. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.

336137.title: The permanent-non-singular $(1,1)$-matrix conjecture
336137.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and orient its edges arbitrarily. Define the graph matrix $A_G$ with rows indexed by $E(G)$ and columns indexed by $V(G)\cup E(G)$ by assigning to an oriented edge $e=(u,v)$ the entries $1$ in the column for $v$ and for edges other than $e$ incident with $v$, $-1$ in the column for $u$ and for edges other than $e$ incident with $u$, and $0$ elsewhere. For an index function $\eta$, let $A_G(\eta)$ repeat the column indexed by $z$ exactly $\eta(z)$ times. An **$(a,b)$-matrix** is a square matrix $A_G(\eta)$ with $\eta(v)\le a$ for every vertex and $\eta(e)\le b$ for every edge; it is **permanent-non-singular** when its permanent is nonzero. **The permanent-non-singular $(1,1)$-matrix conjecture.** Every graph $G$ has a permanent-non-singular $(1,1)$-matrix. This matrix formulation is motivated by total-weighting and edge-weighting problems; the stated status evidence says the conjecture is resolved for wheels and Halin graphs, while no general resolution is supplied here.

336854.title: The tight-star conjecture for betweenness structures
336854.literal_statement:
A **betweenness structure** is a structure whose associated $3$-uniform hypergraph is denoted by $\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{B})$; write $B(n,m)$ for the family of betweenness structures on $n$ points with parameter $m$. A **tight $k$-star** is a $3$-uniform hypergraph that is the, not necessarily edge-disjoint, union of $k$ tight stars on the same ground set. For integers $k\geq 0$ and $c$, let $N_c^k>0$ be a threshold.

**The tight-star conjecture.** For all integers $k\geq 0$ and $c$, there exists a threshold $N_c^k>0$ such that for all $n\geq N_c^k$ and every betweenness structure $\mathcal{B}\in B(n,kn-c)$, the hypergraph $\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{B})$ is a tight $k$-star.

This conjecture proposes extending the paper's characterization of betweenness structures of small linear co-size from the cases treated there to co-size $kn-c$. The stated inequality $\vartheta_{\min}(k)\geq 2k$ is presented as an easy consequence, but no resolution of the conjecture is given here.

By (P4), a triple whose three pairs are all aligned is collinear, so every local triangle contains a non-aligned pair and the non-aligned pairs (exactly k of them) cover H(B). 338235.title: The eventual classification conjecture for Boolean degree 1 functions on Grassmann graphs
338235.literal_statement:
Let $J_q(n,k)$ denote the Grassmann graph of $k$-dimensional subspaces of an $n$-dimensional vector space over the finite field with $q$ elements. A Boolean degree $1$ function is called **trivial** if it is one of the standard functions induced by a constant, a point, a hyperplane, or a point and a hyperplane in the sense described in the paper.

**Eventual Grassmann graph classification conjecture.** Let $q$ be a prime power. Then there exists a constant $n_q$ such that a Boolean degree $1$ function on $J_q(n,k)$ is trivial for all $n\geq n_q$ if $k,n-k\geq 2$.

This predicts that, for each fixed field size, all Boolean degree $1$ functions on Grassmann graphs are eventually among the standard examples as the ambient dimension grows. The paper presents this as a broader conjectural direction beyond the cases it proves.

339497.title: Binary matroid conjecture excluding an independent set and a triangle
339497.literal_statement:
Let $s$ be a positive integer. A **simple binary matroid** is a binary matroid with no loops or parallel elements; an **induced $I_s$-restriction** and an **induced $\operatorname{PG}(1,2)$-restriction** are restrictions isomorphic to the indicated matroids. Write $\chi(M)$ for the chromatic number of a matroid $M$. **Binary matroid chromatic-number conjecture.** For every $s \ge 1$, there exists an integer $k$ such that if $M$ is a simple binary matroid with no induced $I_s$-restriction or $\operatorname{PG}(1,2)$-restriction, then

$$
\chi(M) \le k.
$$

This is the $t=2$ case of the proposed matroidal analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture. The corresponding general matroidal statement is refuted already when $s=t=3$, while this triangle-excluding case remains open; its graph-theoretic analogue is known for stars but open in general.

341257.title: Conditional local moves on polygonal networks for every n
341257.literal_statement:
Let $\Pi_n$ denote the polygonal resistor network used in the paper, and let a conditional local move be a local transformation of a subgraph of $\Pi_n$. Boundary edges and boundary spikes refer to the corresponding outer-boundary features; the outermost layer and outermost partial layer are the layers specified by the construction of $\Pi_n$.

**Conditional local-move existence conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 3$, there exists a conditional local move on $\Pi_n$ such that:

$$
\begin{cases}
 n\equiv 3\pmod 4: & \text{a boundary edge from the outermost layer is changed into a boundary spike on the opposite side};\\
 n\equiv 0\pmod 4: & \text{a boundary spike from the outermost partial layer is changed into a boundary spike on the opposite side};\\
 n\equiv 1\pmod 4: & \text{a boundary spike from the outermost partial layer is changed into a boundary edge on the opposite side};\\
 n\equiv 2\pmod 4: & \text{a boundary edge from the outermost partial layer is changed into a boundary edge on the opposite side}.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture extends the conditional local moves listed earlier and suggests a combinatorial interpretation of their formulas in terms of groves or a grove-like structure. The source gives no proof of existence for all $n$, so the conjecture remains open.

341638.title: Good-relation covering conjecture for individually private information retrieval
341638.literal_statement:
Let $K\geq 1$, $M\geq 1$, and $D\geq 2$ satisfy $D+M\leq K$. Set $\mathcal{K}=[K]$, and let $\mathcal{I}$ and $\mathcal{J}$ be the sets of subsets $I,J\subseteq\mathcal{K}$ with $0\leq |I|\leq M$ and $|J|\geq D$, respectively. A relation $f:\mathcal{I}\to\mathcal{J}$ is **good** if (i) $I\subseteq f(I)$ for every $I\in\mathcal{I}$; (ii) for every $j\in\mathcal{K}$, there are $I\in\mathcal{I}$ and $J\in\mathcal{J}$ with $|J|=D$, $j\in J$, $I\cap J=\emptyset$, and $J\subseteq f(I)$; (iii) if $I_1,I_2\in\mathcal{I}$ and $I_2\subseteq f(I_1)$, then $f(I_2)\subseteq f(I_1)$; and (iv) for every $J^{*}\subseteq\mathcal{K}$ with $|J^{*}|<\lceil K/D\rceil$, there is a non-empty $I\in\mathcal{I}$ such that $f(I)\cap J^{*}=\emptyset$. **Good-relation covering conjecture.** For every good relation $f$, there exists $I^{*}\subseteq\mathcal{K}$ with

$$
|I^{*}|\leq \max\left\{K-D\left\lceil\frac{K}{M+D}\right\rceil,\,M\left\lfloor\frac{K}{M+D}\right\rfloor\right\}
$$

such that

$$
\bigcup_{I\subseteq I^{*}}f(I)=\mathcal{K}.
$$

This covering property would provide a lower bound on the conditional answer entropy of any individually private information retrieval protocol with side information. Its status is not resolved by the supplied text.

Condition (iii) with I_2 = emptyset (always a subset of f(I_1)) gives f(emptyset) a subset of f(I) for every I. Take j_0 in f(emptyset) and J* = {j_0}; since K >= D+M > D we have ceil(K/D) >= 2 > |J*|, so (iv) demands a non-empty I with f(I) disjoint from {j_0}, which is impossible. Hence no good relation exists and the conjecture as printed is vacuously true. Intended version: the authors themselves (Heidarzadeh-Sprintson, ITW 2021, as summarised in arXiv:2202.12229 Sec. I and Remark 2; the ITW 2021 body itself was not retrieved) report that the scheme of [1] is not optimal for D=M=2 (capacity 2/ceil(K/2)). 341639.title: D-graph external mother vertex-set conjecture
341639.literal_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a directed graph without parallel edges on $K$ nodes. For a node $v\in V$, write $d_{\mathrm{in}}(v)$ and $d_{\mathrm{out}}(v)$ for its in-degree and out-degree. An **external mother vertex-set** is a minimal subset $I^{*}\subseteq V$ from which every node outside $I^{*}$ with nonzero out-degree is reachable. Let $\mu_{\mathrm{ext}}(G)$ be its size. Call $G$ a **$D$-graph** if every node has in-degree at least $1$, every node has either out-degree $0$ or out-degree at least $D$, and the internal mother vertex-set size of its transpose satisfies $\mu_{\mathrm{int}}(G^{\mathsf{T}})\geq\lceil K/D\rceil$. **D-graph external mother vertex-set conjecture.** For every $D$-graph $G$ on $K$ nodes,

$$
\mu_{\mathrm{ext}}(G)\leq\left\lfloor\frac{K}{D+1}\right\rfloor.
$$

This is presented as the graph-theoretic formulation for the case $M=1$ of the preceding good-relation conjecture; the supplied text gives no resolution.

343527.title: Generalized weak-subdivision conjecture for complete graphs
343527.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, and let $\overline{G}$ denote its complement. An **induced weak-subdivision of $K_t$** is an induced subgraph of $G$ obtained by the weak-subdivision operation applied to the complete graph $K_t$; a **bi-clique** is a complete bipartite subgraph.

**Generalized weak-subdivision conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$ and integer $t\geq 3$, there exists $\delta>0$ such that, if $G$ has at most

$$
\left(\frac{1}{t-1}-\epsilon\right)\frac{n^{2}}{2}
$$

edges and does not contain an induced weak-subdivision of $K_t$, then $\overline{G}$ contains a bi-clique of size at least $\delta n$.

The conjecture generalizes the proved $K_5$ case discussed immediately beforehand and is stated as sharp in the source: examples formed from $t-1$ clique parts can have nearly the threshold number of edges while their complements have no linear-sized bi-clique. The supplied text does not indicate that the general case has been resolved.

344134.title: Saad–Wolf commonness conjecture for even-variable linear equations
344134.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $k\ge 2$. Consider the linear equation over $\mathbb{F}_q^n$

$$
\na_1x_1+\cdots+a_{2k}x_{2k}=0.
$$

The equation is **common** if, for every two-coloring of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, the number of monochromatic solutions is at least $2^{1-2k}q^{n(2k-1)}$. **Saad–Wolf's conjecture.** The equation is common in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ if and only if the multiset of coefficients $\{a_1,\ldots,a_{2k}\}$ can be partitioned into $k$ pairs, each pair summing to zero. Saad and Wolf proposed this characterization for linear equations with an even number of variables; the paper's abstract states that the authors characterize common linear equations and that their construction disproves some such properties, but the supplied material does not establish the resolution of this exact conjecture.

344227.title: The 6-cover conjecture for flow-admissible signed graphs
344227.literal_statement:
A signed graph $(G,\Sigma)$ consists of a graph $G$ and a set $\Sigma\subseteq E(G)$ of negative edges. A **signed circuit** is either a balanced circuit, containing an even number of edges of $\Sigma$, or a barbell, consisting of two unbalanced circuits sharing exactly one vertex or two vertex-disjoint unbalanced circuits joined by a minimal path. The signed graph is **flow-admissible** if every edge belongs to a signed circuit.

**6-cover conjecture.** Every flow-admissible signed graph has a family of signed circuits such that every edge belongs to exactly $6$ members of the family.

This extends the circuit-cover problem from ordinary bridgeless graphs to signed graphs. It is known that flow-admissible signed graphs with no $k$-cover exist for every positive integer $k\leq 5$; the conjecture asserts that $6$ is sufficient, while its truth remains open.

344586.title: Griggs's dominance conjecture for chain decompositions of the Boolean lattice
344586.literal_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $2^{[n]}$ be the Boolean lattice, and set

$$
M=\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
$$

Let $\sigma_1\geq\dots\geq\sigma_M$ be the sizes of the chains in a symmetric chain decomposition of $2^{[n]}$. A sequence $s_1,\dots,s_M$ is **dominated** by $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_M$ when

$$
\sum_{i=1}^k s_i\leq\sum_{i=1}^k\sigma_i\quad (k=1,\dots,M).
$$

**Griggs's conjecture.** If $s_1\geq\dots\geq s_M$ is a sequence of positive integers dominated by $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_M$ and

$$
\sum_{i=1}^M s_i=2^n,
$$

then there exists a chain decomposition $D_1,\dots,D_M$ of $2^{[n]}$ such that $|D_i|=s_i$ for every $i$.
The conjecture proposes that every admissible chain-size sequence below the symmetric-chain profile can be realized. The source attributes it to Griggs; it notes that the uniform chain decomposition conjecture is a special subcase and may be the most challenging one.

344587.title: Upper-half dominance conjecture for chain decompositions of the Boolean lattice
344587.literal_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $B=[n]^{(\geq n/2)}$ be the family of subsets of $[n]$ of size at least $n/2$, and set

$$
M=\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
$$

Let $\sigma_1\geq\dots\geq\sigma_M$ be the sizes of the chains in a symmetric chain decomposition of $2^{[n]}$, and define

$$
\sigma_i'=\left\lceil\frac{\sigma_i}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

**Upper-half dominance conjecture.** If $s_1\geq\dots\geq s_M$ is a sequence of positive integers dominated by $\sigma_1',\dots,\sigma_M'$ and

$$
\sum_{i=1}^M s_i=|B|,
$$

then there exists a chain decomposition $D_1,\dots,D_M$ of $B$ such that $|D_i|=s_i$ for every $i$.
This is the analogous realization problem for the upper half of the Boolean lattice. The source presents it as a related conjecture to Griggs's conjecture; no resolution is supplied in the provided text.

346758.title: Gallai-Ramsey conjecture for blow-ups of complete graphs
346758.literal_statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ and $m\geq 2$. For a graph $H$, let $GR_k(H)$ denote the least order of a complete graph such that every exact $k$-edge-coloring contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, let $R_2(H)$ be the two-color Ramsey number of $H$, and let $\widehat{K}_m$ denote the graph obtained from $K_m$ by attaching a pendant edge to each vertex. **Gallai-Ramsey conjecture for $\widehat{K}_m$.** One has $GR_1(\widehat{K}_m)=m+1$ and

$$
GR_k(\widehat{K}_m)=
\begin{cases}
(R_2(\widehat{K}_m)-1)\cdot 5^{(k-2)/2}+1, & \text{if $k$ is even and $m$ is odd},\\
R_2(\widehat{K}_m)+(m/2)\cdot(5^{k/2}-5), & \text{if $k$ is even and $m$ is even},\\
\max\{2(R_2(\widehat{K}_m)-1),5m\}\cdot 5^{(k-3)/2}+1, & \text{if $k\geq 3$ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

This extends the known exact values for $\widehat{K}_m$ with $2\leq m\leq 4$ and is motivated by general lower bounds; determining the Gallai-Ramsey numbers for all $m\geq 2$ remains open.

347546.title: The conjecture on spectral separation for rank-one quasinilpotent perturbations
347546.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a quasinilpotent operator. For a positive scalar $m$ chosen so that $4\widetilde{T}=mT4$ has norm $a$, write $4\widetilde{T}=mT4$. Let $F$ be a rank-$1$ quasinilpotent operator with $4\|F\|=b4$, and let $4\sigma_t(A)4$ denote the separated parts of the spectrum at scale $t$; let $B(0,r)$ be the open disk of radius $r$ centered at $0$, and let $4\Phi_{a,b,t,S}(\alpha)4$ be the stated function depending on $4\alpha4$. The conjecture asserts that there exist $a,b,t>0$ such that, for every such $F$ for which $4\widetilde{T}^*+\alpha F4$ is not quasinilpotent for at least two distinct complex values of $4\alpha4$, there is a subset $4S\subseteq\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}4$ with $4|S|\geq24$, possibly depending on $F$, satisfying the following properties: (i) $4\widetilde{T}^*+\alpha F4$ is not quasinilpotent for every $4\alpha\in S4$; and (ii), for every $4\alpha\in S4$,

$$
\sigma_t(\widetilde{T}+\alpha F)\subseteq\sigma(\widetilde{T}+\alpha F)+B(0,\Phi_{a,b,t,S}(\alpha)),
$$

and $4\sigma(\widetilde{T}+\alpha F)+B(0,\Phi_{a,b,t,S}(\alpha))4$ is disconnected in $4\mathbb{C}4$. **Spectral-separation conjecture.** Under these hypotheses, the subset $S$ with both stated properties exists.

348515.title: The colorful fractional Helly conjecture for d-Leray complexes
348515.literal_statement:
A simplicial complex $\mathsf{K}$ is **$d$-Leray** if, for every induced subcomplex $\mathsf{L}\leq\mathsf{K}$ and every $i\ge d$, its reduced homology group $\widetilde H_i(\mathsf{L})$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ vanishes. Let the vertex set be partitioned as $N=N_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup N_{d+1}$, and write $n_i:=|N_i|$ for $i\in[d+1]$. A colorful $d$-face is a $d$-dimensional face containing one vertex from each $N_i$. **The colorful fractional Helly conjecture for $d$-Leray complexes.** If $\mathsf{K}$ contains at least $\alpha n_1\cdots n_{d+1}$ colorful $d$-faces for some $\alpha\in(0,1]$, then there is an $i\in[d+1]$ such that

$$
\dim\mathsf{K}[N_i]\geq\bigl(1-(1-\alpha)^{1/(d+1)}\bigr)n_i-1.
$$

This would extend the proved optimal theorem for $d$-collapsible complexes to the broader class of $d$-Leray complexes, providing a topological analogue of the convex-set result; the source does not report a resolution.

359661.title: Cohen et al.'s general oriented-cycle subdivision conjecture
359661.literal_statement: For positive integers $k_1,k_2,\ldots,k_n$, let $C(k_1,k_2,\ldots,k_n)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by blocks of those lengths. A digraph is **strongly connected** if every ordered pair of vertices is joined by a directed path, and a subdivision is obtained by replacing each arc with a directed path of length at least $1$, with all replacement paths internally disjoint. The chromatic number of a digraph $D$ is denoted by $\chi(D)$. **Cohen et al.'s conjecture.** For every positive integers $k_1,k_2,\ldots,k_n$, there exists a constant $g(k_1,k_2,\ldots,k_n)$ such that every strongly connected digraph containing no subdivisions of the oriented cycle $C(k_1,k_2,\ldots,k_n)$ has chromatic number at most $g(k_1,k_2,\ldots,k_n)$. This conjecture seeks to extend Bondy's theorem from directed cycles to all oriented cycles; the source does not specify a resolution.
